sc: Dull percussion with bronchial breathing → Lobar pneumonia
Trachea shifted away, stony dull, absent breath sounds → Pleural effusion
Clubbing with a chronic productive cough → Bronchiectasis or CF
f: Introduce, consent, expose · general look · hands (clubbing), RR, SpO2 · inspection · palpation (trachea, expansion) · percussion · auscultation · back
Consolidation: dull, bronchial breathing, crackles · effusion: stony dull, trachea away · collapse: trachea towards · wheeze: asthma, bronchiolitis
Nasal flaring, grunting, chest indrawing, head bobbing, tracheal tug
Positive findings first, then relevant negatives, then the likely diagnosis
Chest X-ray · SpO2 · CBC · sputum/gastric aspirate (TB) · sweat test (CF)
Count RR for a full minute · warm hands · examine the back · ENT in every chest station
trap: Fast breathing is the best sign of pneumonia in young children · trachea towards the dull side = collapse, away = effusion
